nodes.title: subject_definitions
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> (<Picture 1>, <Picture 2>, <Picture 3>): Maya, a woman in her late twenties with warm brown skin, dark shoulder-length curls parted on the left, and a small mole under her right eye. She wears an oversized cream ribbed sweater. <Picture 1> is her three-quarter view holding the product, <Picture 2> her straight-on close-up, <Picture 3> her profile.
<Subject 2> (<Picture 1>): the product, a 50 ml frosted-glass jar with a matte white screw lid and one line of thin black serif type reading "AURELIE".
<Subject 3>: the room, a small apartment bathroom with white subway tile, a round brass-framed mirror, and one window camera-left throwing soft overcast daylight across her face.

nodes.title: retention_analysis
widgets_values:
retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2]): fully_preserved - face geometry, the mole under the right eye, the curl pattern and hair part, and the cream ribbed sweater carry across both shots unchanged.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2]): fully_preserved - jar proportions, matte white lid and the "AURELIE" label type stay identical, and the label stays legible and correctly spelled at every distance.
<Subject 3> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2]): attribute_transfer - the tile, mirror and window light of <Picture 1> carry into both shots; the camera position and framing change, the room does not.

nodes.title: non_diegetic_music
widgets_values:
non_diegetic_music:
A single nylon-string guitar figure at roughly 80 BPM, plucked in steady eighth notes with a soft brushed shaker on the offbeat. It enters under the first line, holds flat through the cut, and drops about 6 dB under the second line.

nodes.title: summary
widgets_values:
summary:
Maya sets the jar down on the sink ledge and tells the camera what changed for her skin, then the shot cuts closer as she twists the lid open and shows the texture on her fingertip.

nodes.title: detailed_description
widgets_values:
detailed_description:
[Shot 1] Medium shot, waist up, <Subject 1> centered with the brass mirror behind her left shoulder. She sets <Subject 2> down on the tile ledge with her right hand, looks into the lens and speaks. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed across the whole shot. (S1) says: <d>[English] Okay, three weeks in, and I finally have to talk about this one.</d>
[Shot 2] At 00:06.000, the camera cuts to a close-up of her hands and the lower half of her face. She twists the matte white lid off <Subject 2>, tips the jar toward the lens and presses one fingertip into the cream. The camera tilts down with medium amplitude at slow speed to follow her hands, then holds. (S1) says: <d>[English] It is thicker than it looks, you barely need this much.</d>

nodes.title: overall_soundscape
widgets_values:
overall_soundscape:
Close, dry indoor room tone with the faint hum of a bathroom fan. The glass jar sets down on the tile with one short hard tap in [Shot 1]. In [Shot 2] the lid gives a fine gritty twist as it unthreads, and the cream makes a soft wet press under her fingertip. She takes a short audible breath in before her second line.

nodes.title: FL2VA image-alignment line
widgets_values: Match the given first frame exactly: same person, same face, same wardrobe, same product and label, same room and lighting. Continue the motion out of that frame — do not restage, recast or relight. Treat the summary and detailed_description below as one integrated_multimodal_description.

nodes.title: Last frame → pick this in First frame for FL2VA
How to use
widgets_values:
# MiniMax H3 — multi-shot UGC beat

One Run makes **one beat**: a single 12-second clip that may contain several
shots, with native synced audio — voice, room sound and music generated in one
pass. Render beat after beat, then stitch them with the assemble workflow.

## The loop

1. Fill the **Casting** boxes once — who the person is, what the product is,
   what the room is. You never retype these.
2. Fill the **This beat** boxes — summary, shot list, soundscape.
3. Run. You get `beat_00001_.mp4` and `lastframe_00001_.png`.
4. For beat 2, change only the **This beat** boxes and Run again.

## Two modes, one switch

The green **Mode** node picks the model:

- **off = Ref2VA** (default) — your reference images, and optionally a
  reference video and a voice clip, feed the model. **Use this for anything
  with dialogue.**
- **on = FL2VA** — first-frame / last-frame interpolation. This mode has **no
  reference-audio path, so it re-rolls the speaker**: the voice changes between
  beats. Use it for action and B-roll only.

The switch is lazy, so only the selected checkpoint is ever loaded. That is why
both 19.5 GB models can ship in one graph.

## Continuity between beats

The **Continuity** group is bypassed. From beat 2 onward select its two nodes,
press Ctrl+B to un-bypass, and point `LoadVideo` at your **hero beat** — the
beat whose look every other beat should match.

**Always point it at the hero beat, never at the newest one.** Chaining beat N
from beat N−1 compounds artifacts on every generation; every beat referencing
beat 1 does not.

## Outputs

`beat` — the clip. `lastframe` — the final frame as a PNG, written on every
Run with no interaction.

Every image slot in this graph ships pointing at the one example photo the
launch script seeds, so the first Queue works with zero uploads. That is the
only reason **First frame** starts there — it is not a meaningful default. Once
Run 1 has written a `lastframe_00001_.png`, pick that from its dropdown before
you switch to FL2VA, and replace `<Picture 2>` / `<Picture 3>` with other
angles of the same person before you un-bypass them.

nodes.title: Prompting — the six boxes
widgets_values:
# The six boxes

H3 reads a structured prompt. Each box already opens with its own section
label, so assembly is a plain join — **never delete the first line of a box.**

Aim for **350–500 words across all six boxes together**. An under-written
prompt is the single most common cause of identity drift.

## Casting — set once, never retype

**subject_definitions** — bind each `<Subject N>` to the `<Picture N>` slots
that show it. One subject may cite several pictures, and that is exactly what
holds a face across a cut. Wardrobe, product and room go here too.

**retention_analysis** — the identity lever. One line per subject:

    <Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2]): fully_preserved - ...
    <Subject 3> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2]): attribute_transfer - ...

`fully_preserved` means do not change it. `attribute_transfer` means carry the
look across; framing may change.

**non_diegetic_music** — instrumentation, speed, rhythm, dynamics. Concrete
only: *nylon-string guitar, 80 BPM, plucked eighths, drops 6 dB under the
second line*. Not "warm", not "uplifting". Write `N/A` for no score.

## This beat — retype every Run

**summary** — one or two lines. What happens in this beat.

**detailed_description** — the shot list, and the box that does the work:

    [Shot 1] ...
    [Shot 2] At 00:06.000, the camera cuts to ...

Write every camera move as **motion type + amplitude + speed** — "pushes in
with small amplitude at slow speed", "tilts down with medium amplitude at slow
speed". Write dialogue as `(S1) says: <d>[English] ...</d>`.

**overall_soundscape** — 1 to 4 sentences across the whole beat: ambience,
physical action sound, non-verbal human sound such as a breath or a laugh.

## Voice lock

Un-bypass **Voice lock** and upload 5–10 s of clean speech to pin a voice to a
character. The binding in the prompt is `<Audio 1>` tied to a speaker id:

    <Subject 1> (S1) speaks with the voice in <Audio 1>.
    (S1) says: <d>[English] ...</d>

This holds a voice far more reliably than inheriting one from a reference video.

reads the URLs out of this graph, so a loader without a URL is a missing file.

nodes.title: Read before flipping
widgets_values:
### Before you flip this

**off = Ref2VA** (default) — reference images, reference video and reference
audio all feed the model. Keeps the face **and the voice**.

**on = FL2VA** — first frame to last frame. It has **no reference-audio input,
so it re-rolls the speaker**: the voice changes. Use it for action and B-roll,
never for a beat with dialogue.

The switch is lazy — the branch you did not select never executes, so the other
checkpoint is never loaded.

nodes.title: Turbo recipe
widgets_values:
### Turbo LoRA — bypassed on purpose

About 2.5x faster, off by default because it trades against this template's
headline feature. At **4 steps** the stock sampler produces severe audio
clipping and noise; at **8 steps** output is usable but slightly below
20-step quality.

Recipe: un-bypass this node (Ctrl+B) → Basic Scheduler `steps` 8 →
`sampler` euler → `scheduler` simple → `strength` 1.0.

The file downloads whether the node is bypassed or not, so un-bypassing never
fails on a missing weight.

nodes.title: Why sigma shift
widgets_values:
### Sigma shift

Sits **after** the model switch, so it applies to whichever checkpoint is live.
This is the dual-clock schedule that makes the turbo LoRA usable at 8 steps.
Requires a ComfyUI image newer than `bdcb886`.

nodes.title: Size, length and VRAM
widgets_values:
### Size and length

**0.8 MP / 9:16** gives H3 a 672x1184 portrait canvas, rounded to 32 — the
proven-fast default. **1.0 MP** reaches H3's native cap of 768x1344, the
768 px short edge.

**Duration 12 s** feeds the frame-grid expression and lands on length **294**.
H3 tops out around 15 s of useful output.

12 s at 0.8 MP is the target on a 24 GB card. On OOM drop to **0.4 MP before
you shorten the beat** — a shorter beat costs you a seam, a smaller canvas only
costs detail.

`ref_image_size` on the Ref2VA node is set to **max** (up to a 2048 px short
edge) because UGC lives on face and product-label fidelity. Switch it to
**match** for fast drafts; reference tokens ride along every sampling step.

groups.title: Models — both ship, only the selected one loads
Mode — Ref2VA for dialogue · FL2VA for action
Turbo LoRA — ~2.5x faster: un-bypass, set steps to 8
Sigma shift — applies to whichever model is live
Prompt assembly — nothing to set here
Size & length — shared by both modes
Casting — three angles of the SAME person: replace 2 and 3 before un-bypassing
Continuity — un-bypass from beat 2 onward, always point at the hero beat
Voice lock — upload 5-10 s of clean speech
FL2VA — first/last frame, re-rolls the speaker
First frame — after Run 1, pick a lastframe_....png from this dropdown
Target frame — un-bypass to interpolate A to B
